title: Fallen Studios | Flight 15: The Catch From Orbit

brief.prompt: Create an original, stunning but faithful 45-second cinematic engineering reconstruction of the NOVEMBER 14 2026 SpaceX Ship 42 upper-stage return and first Starship upper-stage catch at Starbase Texas. THIS IS A RECONSTRUCTION, NOT ACTUAL VIDEO. Lead with the terrifying scale of a stainless upper-stage spacecraft moving through dusk clouds toward Mechazilla; cut to 3D cross-sectional geometry and an orbital-flight line; reveal black thermal tiles, control flaps, orbital reentry plasma, near-vertical descent, final engine braking and the two huge mechanical arms gently supporting the upper stage. Animate physically plausible relative scale and camera moves, NOT an unsupported engineering simulation or raw actual flight telemetry. Clearly separate Ship 42 from Super Heavy: do not show a booster being caught; the booster recovery ABORTED. Include a 2-second reality check at the end explaining no full-vehicle recovery was achieved. Source facts from SpaceX mission page, AP and AIAA. Logo and title elegant, editorial, not clickbait. No borrowed soundtrack or false footage claims; original score only. Voiceover warm, expressive and accurate only if a legitimately authorized voice model or performer is available, otherwise leave dialogue as a planned unrendered track. Export 9:16 with a separate 16:9 master. Do not publish unless visual provenance, rights, Systemia release and Clip receipts pass.
brief.audience: Curious science and engineering readers on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube Shorts and Evercraft Journal
brief.cta: Read the source-backed breakdown on Evercraft Journal AFTER the canonical public URL is verified
brief.style: Fallen Studios cinematic documentary explainer; dimensional scale, original 3D modeling, real atmospheric light and precise mechanical detail; no neon text-card montage; labels readable on phone
